title: [R11][C] Exact same-unit FiberGuard decision value on ASlib SAT12-ALL
body:
This child turns the R10 action-regret/conflict-certificate theory into a real public algorithm-selection discriminator using a pinned ASlib scenario where solver runtime and feature-acquisition cost are recorded in the same unit.

## Frozen corpus

- upstream: `coseal/aslib_data`
- commit: `551b22beef8df17de59286b4822ef720e0aa4d6f`
- scenario: `SAT12-ALL`
- exact Git blobs are content-bound for description, algorithm runs, feature values, feature costs and feature runstatus before evaluation.

## Exact experiment

For every dependency-closed feature-step subset, the audit forms exact representation fibres from observed ASlib feature values plus step runstatus. For each fibre it chooses one solver minimizing worst-case

`feature acquisition time + solver PAR10 runtime - statewise virtual-best runtime`.

Because ASlib supplies both algorithm and feature-step runtimes, this avoids the arbitrary regret/feature-cost scalarization that blocked the earlier application formulation. All alternatives share one statewise oracle baseline.

The audit evaluates every dependency-closed representation, reports no-feature/all-feature/static-optimal baselines, action-only regret, robust total excess, mean/median/p95 total excess, and the full cost/regret Pareto surface. Every worst fibre also emits an exact compressed witness of size at most the 31-action portfolio size, instantiating the R10 witness-compression theorem on a real solver portfolio.

## Reproducibility

A path-scoped workflow sparse-fetches the exact upstream commit, verifies all registered Git blob IDs, runs the audit twice, requires byte-identical JSON, checks fail-closed authority flags, and uploads an immutable result artifact.

## Authority boundary

This is corpus-complete static decision evidence only. It does not claim unseen-instance generalization, learned-selector superiority, production deployment value, or journal authority. A null result is first-class evidence. The adaptive answer/refine/defer study is a later tranche after this static same-unit discriminator is frozen.

title: [R11][D] Certify real agentgateway authorization merge as origin-witness safe
body:
This child gives Paper D a real external **SAFE** control rather than another hostile synthetic example.

Pinned source: `agentgateway/agentgateway@e136c7458b0fe0f51378dd31ffd60ab2b6939fc2`, with exact Git blobs bound for API validation, policy selection, traffic translation, runtime policy merge, backend merge, HTTP authorization and MCP RBAC.

## Source-derived theorem

For each authorization origin i define request-relative Boolean summaries:
- `D_i`: some deny matches;
- `R_i`: all requires match;
- `H_i`: an allowlist exists;
- `A_i`: some allow matches.

The exact `RuleSets` semantics are

`Accept_i = !D_i && R_i && (!H_i || A_i)`

and merged semantics concatenate rule sets, giving

`Accept_merge = (all !D_i) && (all R_i) && ((all !H_i) || (some A_i))`.

Therefore:

1. a merged allow cannot launder any constituent deny or failed require;
2. **origin-witness preservation**: every merged allow is already allowed by at least one constituent origin, so this merge operator has no Paper-D hybrid witness of the form “merge authorizes but no selected origin authorizes”;
3. the merge is intentionally not intersection semantics—disjoint allowlists union—but no authority appears without an allowing origin;
4. acceptance semantics are associative, commutative and duplicate-idempotent;
5. MCP authorization inherits the theorem because it delegates to the same `RuleSets::merge`.

The upstream MCP test already checks the key null control: a higher-precedence allow does not erase a base deny.

## Finite corroboration

A separate standard-library verifier exhausts five request-relative origin states through eight origins and checks the closed form, witness property, mandatory constraints, semantic algebra, a non-intersection control, base-deny/higher-allow, and failed-require laundering.

## Scientific boundary

This certifies one same-field merge algebra, not the whole gateway. Cross-field modular composition (for example identity claims consumed by authorization) must be represented by explicit bridge licenses; Paper D must not call intentional modularity “splicing” merely because multiple configuration documents contribute.

This real SAFE result improves specificity of the D method and complements the RFC-grounded synthetic false-authorization corpus.
